questions.question: In May 2025, iPhone maker Foxconn announced to invest how much amount in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**US$ 1.5 billion**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Foxconn**, the renowned Taiwanese electronics manufacturer and a key supplier for Apple's iPhones, announced a plan to invest **US$ 1.5 billion** in India in **May 2025**.
 
• This investment is aimed at expanding Foxconn's production facilities in India, which aligns with the Indian government's push to strengthen the **domestic electronics manufacturing ecosystem**.
 
• The move is expected to generate thousands of **new job opportunities** and bolster India's position in the global supply chain for consumer electronics.
 
• Foxconn's decision to invest in India is part of its strategy to diversify manufacturing locations outside China amid ongoing geopolitical tensions and to leverage India’s **Production Linked Incentive (PLI)** schemes.
 
• This large-scale investment reflects the growing importance of India as a manufacturing hub for global electronics companies and highlights the government's efforts to attract foreign direct investment (FDI).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Foxconn Overview:**

 
 
• Foxconn, officially known as **Hon Hai Precision Industry Co., Ltd.**, is a Taiwanese multinational electronics contract manufacturer.
 
• It is one of the world's largest producers of electronics and semiconductors, manufacturing for major brands like **Apple, Sony, Dell, and Microsoft**.
 
• Foxconn has been operating in India for several years, with existing manufacturing facilities in states like **Tamil Nadu**.
 
 
 
• **India’s Electronics Manufacturing Push:**
 
 
• The Indian government has introduced various **Production Linked Incentive (PLI) schemes** to promote domestic electronics manufacturing and attract foreign investors.
 
• India aims to become a global electronics manufacturing hub, focusing on sectors such as **smartphones, semiconductors, and consumer electronics**.
 
• Major global players like Samsung, Xiaomi, and Apple have already established manufacturing operations in India.
 
 
 
• **Significance of Foxconn's Investment:**
 
 
• Foxconn's investment of **US$ 1.5 billion** in India is expected to enhance the country's capabilities in **high-tech manufacturing**.
 
• The initiative aligns with the government’s “**Make in India**” campaign, which promotes domestic production and reduces dependency on imports.
 
• This investment is likely to strengthen India’s position as a preferred destination for **electronics manufacturing** in Asia.
 
 
 
• **Global Geopolitical Context:**
 
 
• Foxconn’s diversification strategy comes amid **geopolitical tensions** between the US and China, prompting companies to explore alternative manufacturing hubs.
 
• India, with its **favorable policies** and skilled labor force, is increasingly becoming a preferred choice for companies looking to reduce reliance on China.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Production Linked Incentive (PLI) Scheme:**

 
 
• Introduced in **2020**, the PLI scheme aims to boost domestic manufacturing by providing incentives to companies.
 
• It covers sectors like electronics, pharmaceuticals, automobiles, and textiles, encouraging global companies to establish manufacturing units in India.
 
• PLI schemes have attracted significant investments from global giants, including Apple suppliers like **Foxconn, Wistron, and Pegatron**.
 
 
 
• **India’s Electronics Market:**
 
 
• The electronics market in India is projected to reach **US$ 400 billion** by **2025**, driven by increasing demand for smartphones, laptops, and other consumer electronics.
 
• India ranks among the top five smartphone markets globally and is a key destination for electronics manufacturing.
 
 
 
• **Foxconn’s Expansion Plans:**
 
 
• Foxconn is exploring other opportunities in India, including the possibility of manufacturing **semiconductors** and expanding its supply chain network.
 
• Its investment in India is expected to have a ripple effect, encouraging other global players to invest in the region.

questions.question: As notified in April 2025, how many new species of Sericinae scarab beetles from the biodiversity-rich regions of India were discovered by Zoological Survey of India in collaboration with Germany’s Museum A. Koenig?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**6**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The discovery of **six new species** of Sericinae scarab beetles was announced in **April 2025**.
 
• This discovery was made by the **Zoological Survey of India (ZSI)** in collaboration with **Germany’s Museum A. Koenig**.
 
• The newly discovered species were found in the **biodiversity-rich regions of India**, which include areas known for their high ecological diversity and unique habitats.
 
• These beetles belong to the subfamily **Sericinae**, which is part of the scarab beetle family (Scarabaeidae).
 
• The discovery highlights the importance of collaborative efforts in documenting biodiversity and conserving it for future generations.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Sericinae Scarab Beetles:**

 
 
• The subfamily Sericinae is part of the Scarabaeidae family, which contains a wide variety of beetles commonly known as scarabs.
 
• These beetles are known for their shiny, metallic appearance and are often found in soil, feeding on organic matter.
 
• Their ecological role includes helping in the decomposition of organic material and nutrient recycling.
 
 
 
• **Zoological Survey of India (ZSI):**
 
 
• The ZSI was established in **1916** to promote the survey, exploration, and research on the fauna of India.
 
• It is headquartered in **Kolkata** and functions under the Ministry of Environment, Forest, and Climate Change.
 
• The ZSI is instrumental in documenting India’s biodiversity and plays a key role in conservation strategies.
 
 
 
• **Collaboration with Museum A. Koenig:**
 
 
• Germany’s Museum A. Koenig is a renowned institution for zoological research and houses vast collections of animal specimens.
 
• The collaboration signifies the importance of international partnerships in advancing scientific knowledge and biodiversity conservation.
 
 
 
• **Biodiversity-rich regions of India:**
 
 
• India is one of the **megadiverse countries**, hosting a significant portion of the world’s flora and fauna.
 
• Regions such as the **Western Ghats, Eastern Himalayas, and Northeast India** are known for their rich biodiversity and endemic species.
 
• These areas are crucial for ecological research and conservation efforts.

questions.question: According to the January 2025 draft rules of the Digital Personal Data Protection Rules (DPDP) Act, children under what age require parental consent to join social media platforms?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**16 years**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• According to the **January 2025 draft rules** of the **Digital Personal Data Protection Rules (DPDP) Act**, children under the age of **16 years** require parental consent to access or join social media platforms.
 
• This measure aims to **protect minors** from harmful content and ensure their safety online.
 
• The **Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023** is designed to regulate the usage of personal data and provides guidelines for **data protection** for individuals, especially vulnerable groups like children.
 
• Parental consent is mandatory for children below **16 years** to ensure accountability and provide oversight for their activities on social media.
 
• The draft rules also emphasize the importance of **age verification mechanisms** to assist platforms in identifying users below the specified age.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023:**

 
 
• Enacted to protect the **privacy** and **security** of individuals' personal data, including special provisions for children.
 
• The act introduces measures to prevent misuse of data and ensures **transparency** in its processing.
 
• It applies to the processing of personal data within India and abroad if it involves offering goods or services to individuals in India.
 
 
 
• **Age Verification Mechanisms:**
 
 
• Social media platforms are required to implement mechanisms to verify the **age** of users to prevent children under the age of **16 years** from joining without parental consent.
 
• These mechanisms ensure compliance with the law and reduce the exposure of minors to inappropriate content.
 
 
 
• **Role of Parents:**
 
 
• Parents play a critical role in overseeing their children's online activities and providing **consent** for social media usage.
 
• They are encouraged to educate their children about **safe online practices** and monitor their interactions on digital platforms.
 
 
 
• **Global Context:**
 
 
• Many countries have similar provisions regarding age restrictions for social media usage. For example, in the **United States**, the **Children's Online Privacy Protection Act (COPPA)** sets the age limit for online activities to **13 years**.
 
• In the **European Union**, the **General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR)** establishes a default age limit of **16 years** for consent in digital services.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Implementation Challenges:** Social media platforms must develop robust **age verification technologies** to comply with the law while ensuring user experience remains seamless.
 
• **Awareness Campaigns:** Government and NGOs need to launch campaigns to educate parents and children about the importance of **safe digital practices** and adhering to age restrictions.
 
• **Penalty for Non-Compliance:** Platforms failing to adhere to the rules may face **legal penalties** under the DPDP Act, ensuring accountability in implementation.

questions.question: Which of the following teams set the 4x100m relay record at the National Relay Carnival 2025?

Archana, Dhanalakshmi, Manikanta Hoblidar and Amlan Borgohain

• Each member of the team has a strong athletic background:
 
 
• **Gurindervir Singh** is known for his explosive starts and is considered one of India’s premier sprinters.
 
• **Animesh Kujur** has consistently performed in national-level competitions and is celebrated for his endurance and speed.
 
• **Manikanta Hoblidar** is recognized for his smooth transitions and reliability in relay events.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• **National Relay Carnival:**

 
 
• The National Relay Carnival is an annual event that aims to promote relay races and bring together the best athletes from across the country.
 
• It serves as a platform for talent identification and preparation for international competitions such as the Asian Games and Olympics.
 
• The carnival includes a variety of relay events, including the **4x100m**, **4x400m**, and mixed relay categories.
 
 
 
• **Importance of Relay Events:**
 
 
• Relay races require excellent coordination among team members, precise baton exchanges, and strategic planning.
 
• They test not just individual speed but also teamwork and collective effort.
 
• Relay events are a prominent part of global athletic competitions like the **Olympics** and **IAAF World Championships**.
 
 
 
• **Indian Athletics Development:**
 
 
• India has made significant strides in athletics, with increasing investments in training facilities, coaching, and international exposure.
 
• Initiatives like the **Target Olympic Podium Scheme (TOPS)** have been instrumental in nurturing athletic talent.
 
• Indian sprinters, including those in relay teams, have started to make their presence felt in international events.
 
 
 
• **Notable Achievements in Indian Relay History:**
 
 
• India’s relay teams have consistently performed well in regional competitions like the **Asian Games**.
 
• With the emergence of athletes like **Amlan Borgohain** and others, the country is poised to challenge world records in relay events.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Team Composition:** The selection of relay team members is based on individual performances, compatibility, and reliability during baton exchanges.
 
• **Training Regimen:** Relay teams undergo specialized training focusing on baton exchange techniques, race strategies, and synchronization.
 
• **Global Standards:** India’s relay teams are striving to meet international standards, with time benchmarks set by leading countries like the USA and Jamaica.
 
• **Future Prospects:** With continued investment and focus, Indian relay teams have the potential to excel in global competitions and bring laurels to the nation.

questions.question: In June 2025, up to what loan amount did the Reserve Bank of India raise the Loan-to-Value (LTV) ratio on gold loans from 75% to 85%?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**₹2.5 lakhs**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• In **June 2025**, the **Reserve Bank of India (RBI)** raised the **Loan-to-Value (LTV) ratio** on gold loans from **75%** to **85%** for loans up to ₹**2.5 lakhs**.
 
• The decision was taken to provide greater liquidity to borrowers, particularly in rural and semi-urban areas where gold loans are prevalent.
 
• The LTV ratio indicates the maximum percentage of the gold's market value that can be provided as a loan. An increase from 75% to 85% means borrowers can avail a higher loan amount against the same quantity of gold.
 
• This measure aimed to support individuals and businesses in need of short-term credit during economic challenges or financial stress.
 
• Gold loans are a popular credit option in India due to their quick processing, minimal documentation, and lower interest rates compared to unsecured loans.

questions.question: As per the India Justice Report, 2025, (which presents a comprehensive assessment of the capacity and performance of Indian states in delivering justice) which of the following states ranked top among small states?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Sikkim**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **India Justice Report (2025)** is an initiative to assess the **capacity and performance of Indian states in delivering justice**. It evaluates states on four pillars: police, judiciary, legal aid, and prisons.
 
• Among the **small states** category (states with a population less than 1 crore), **Sikkim** was ranked as the top-performing state.
 
• The report considers key parameters such as the **state's budget utilization, diversity in police force, infrastructure, vacancies, and legal aid services** to rank states.
 
• **Sikkim's performance** was particularly notable due to its high levels of investment in judicial and legal infrastructure, efficient legal aid mechanisms, and strong representation of women in the police and judiciary.
 
• The report highlights **Sikkim’s commitment to justice delivery** through its effective utilization of funds, low vacancy rates, and focus on inclusivity and access.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **India Justice Report:**

 
 
• The **India Justice Report** is published by the **Tata Trusts** in collaboration with several organizations like the Centre for Social Justice, Common Cause, and the Commonwealth Human Rights Initiative.
 
• It ranks states based on data collected from government sources, including the **National Crime Records Bureau (NCRB), Bureau of Police Research and Development (BPR&D), and court performance data**.
 
• The report aims to **promote transparency, accountability, and improvements** in the justice delivery system across India.
 
 
 
• **Performance of Small States:**
 
 
• Small states are categorized separately due to their **lower population** and unique challenges in governance and resource allocation.
 
• In the 2025 report, **Sikkim** outperformed other small states like **Goa, Nagaland, and Manipur** due to its focus on judicial infrastructure and police modernization.
 
• Other states like **Goa** and **Manipur** also performed well but lagged in specific areas such as legal aid and filling vacancies.
 
 
 
• **Justice Delivery Challenges in India:**
 
 
• **High Pendency of Cases:** India has a significant backlog of cases in courts, which affects timely justice delivery.
 
• **Vacancies in Judiciary:** Many positions in the judiciary remain unfilled, leading to delays in case hearings and judgments.
 
• **Lack of Legal Aid Awareness:** Although free legal aid is available, many citizens are unaware of their rights and entitlements.
 
• **Infrastructure Deficiencies:** Several states face challenges in terms of infrastructure, particularly in lower courts and rural areas.
 
 
 
• **Sikkim's Key Strengths:**
 
 
• **Efficient Budget Utilization:** Sikkim effectively utilizes its allocated budget for police, judiciary, and prison reforms.
 
• **Gender Representation:** Sikkim has a higher percentage of women in its police force and judiciary compared to other small states.
 
• **Access to Legal Aid:** The state has implemented robust mechanisms to ensure that marginalized communities have access to free legal aid.
 
• **Low Vacancy Rates:** The state has one of the lowest vacancy rates in its judiciary and police force, ensuring smoother functioning of justice delivery systems.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Comparison with Other States:** Goa was ranked second among small states, while Nagaland and Manipur followed. The rankings highlight the variations in justice delivery performance among states with similar population sizes.
 
• **National Average:** The India Justice Report also provides insights into the national average performance in areas like police modernization, prison reforms, and judiciary vacancies, enabling states to benchmark their performance.
 
• **Impact of the Report:** By identifying gaps and areas for improvement, the India Justice Report serves as a tool for policymakers to enhance justice delivery in their respective states.
 
• **Significance of Justice Delivery:** An efficient justice system ensures **rule of law, social stability, and economic growth**. States like Sikkim set an example for others to follow.

questions.question: Which of the following bodies implemented the 'UPI for International Transactions' pilot in 2025?

options.text: Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI)

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**National Payments Corporation of India (NPCI)**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **National Payments Corporation of India (NPCI)** is the organization responsible for implementing the **Unified Payments Interface (UPI)** system in India and initiating its pilot for **international transactions in 2025**.
 
• The NPCI launched the pilot program to extend UPI's reach beyond India's borders, enabling seamless **cross-border payments** and fostering global financial inclusion.
 
• The objective of this initiative was to integrate UPI with international payment networks, allowing users to perform transactions abroad using UPI.
 
• Through this pilot, the NPCI aimed to enhance the **acceptability and interoperability** of UPI with global payment systems, paving the way for its widespread adoption internationally.
 
• The NPCI's efforts align with India's ambition to position its **digital payment infrastructure** as a global standard for financial innovation and inclusion.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **National Payments Corporation of India (NPCI):**

 
 
• The NPCI was established in **2008** as an initiative by the **Reserve Bank of India (RBI)** and the **Indian Banks' Association (IBA)** to create a robust payment and settlement infrastructure in the country.
 
• It is a **not-for-profit organization** and serves as the umbrella entity for operating retail payments and settlement systems in India.
 
• NPCI is the driving force behind several innovative payment systems, including **UPI, RuPay, Bharat Bill Payment System (BBPS),** and **Aadhaar Enabled Payment System (AePS)**.
 
 
 
• **Unified Payments Interface (UPI):**
 
 
• UPI is a real-time payment system that facilitates the transfer of money between bank accounts using a mobile platform.
 
• It was launched in **2016** by NPCI and has since become one of the most widely used digital payment platforms in India.
 
• The UPI system supports features such as **P2P (peer-to-peer) transfers**, **bill payments**, and **merchant transactions**.
 
• In recent years, UPI has achieved remarkable success, processing billions of transactions monthly and contributing significantly to India's digital economy.
 
 
 
• **UPI for International Transactions:**
 
 
• In 2025, the NPCI implemented a pilot project to extend UPI's functionality for **international transactions**.
 
• The aim was to enable Indian users to make payments in foreign countries and allow international users to access India's UPI framework.
 
• The system integrates with foreign payment networks and complies with global standards for **cross-border financial transactions**.
 
 
 
• **Other Relevant Organizations:**
 
 
• **Reserve Bank of India (RBI):** The RBI regulates and oversees financial systems in India but delegates operational tasks like UPI implementation to NPCI.
 
• **Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI):** SEBI is responsible for regulating securities markets and does not manage payment systems.
 
• **Central Board of Direct Taxes (CBDT):** The CBDT oversees direct taxation policies and administration in India and has no role in payment infrastructure development.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Collaboration for Cross-Border Payments:**

 
 
• NPCI International Payments Limited (NIPL), a subsidiary of NPCI, spearheaded collaborations with international entities to expand UPI's reach globally.
 
• Countries like **Singapore, UAE, and Bhutan** have already adopted UPI-based systems or are in the process of integrating them.
 
 
 
• **India's Digital Payment Ecosystem:**
 
 
• India is one of the global leaders in digital payments, with systems like UPI, RuPay, and AePS contributing to its success.
 
• Efforts to globalize UPI highlight India's commitment to sharing its technological innovations on an international scale.

questions.question: Which year was declared as the ‘Year of Reforms’ by the Ministry of Defence of the Government of India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**2025**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The Ministry of Defence, Government of India, declared the year **2025** as the "**Year of Reforms**" to bring transformative changes in the defense sector.
 
• This declaration aims to align the defense sector with modern needs, focusing on **self-reliance (Atmanirbhar Bharat)** and enhancing operational efficiency.
 
• One of the primary goals is to implement reforms that boost **indigenous production** of defense equipment under the **Make in India** initiative.
 
• The Ministry is also working towards improving the **ease of doing business** in the defense sector by simplifying procurement processes and enhancing transparency.
 
• Several reforms under the "**Year of Reforms**" initiative include upgrading defense manufacturing capabilities, increasing private sector participation, and modernizing the armed forces.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Atmanirbhar Bharat in Defense:**

 
 
• The **Atmanirbhar Bharat Abhiyan** (Self-Reliant India campaign) was launched by the Government of India in **2020** to promote self-reliance in various sectors, including defense.
 
• It focuses on reducing reliance on imports and enhancing indigenous defense manufacturing capabilities.
 
• Key initiatives include the **Defence Acquisition Procedure (DAP) 2020**, which prioritizes indigenous procurement.
 
 
 
• **Make in India in Defense:**
 
 
• The **Make in India** initiative, launched in **2014**, aims to develop India as a global manufacturing hub, including in the defense sector.
 
• The government has introduced several policy measures to encourage domestic production, such as the **Strategic Partnership Model**.
 
• Examples include the production of **Tejas Light Combat Aircraft (LCA)** and other indigenous defense equipment.
 
 
 
• **Modernization of Armed Forces:**
 
 
• The Ministry of Defence has been focusing on modernizing the armed forces to enhance operational readiness and combat capability.
 
• Modernization plans include procurement of advanced fighter jets, submarines, and artillery systems.
 
• Efforts are being made to ensure the armed forces are equipped with state-of-the-art technology and equipment.
 
 
 
• **Defence Procurement Policy:**
 
 
• The **Defence Procurement Policy (DPP)**, now known as the **Defence Acquisition Procedure (DAP)**, is a key framework for procurement in the defense sector.
 
• DAP 2020 emphasizes **indigenization**, encourages private sector participation, and aims to reduce procurement timelines.
 
• It also includes measures to boost research and development in defense technology.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Defense Exports:**

 
 
• The Government of India has set an ambitious target to achieve **defense exports worth $5 billion** by 2025 as part of its self-reliance goals.
 
• India is promoting indigenous defense products such as the **BrahMos missile system** and **Akash surface-to-air missiles** in the global market.
 
 
 
• **Defense Corridors:**
 
 
• The government has established two dedicated **defense corridors** in **Uttar Pradesh** and **Tamil Nadu** to boost indigenous production and attract investment.
 
• These corridors aim to create a robust defense manufacturing ecosystem and generate employment opportunities.
 
 
 
• **Innovation for Defence Excellence (iDEX):**
 
 
• The **iDEX initiative** was launched to foster innovation and technology development in the defense sector.
 
• It encourages startups and MSMEs to develop solutions for defense and aerospace challenges.
 
• iDEX has significantly contributed to the development of cutting-edge technologies for the Indian armed forces.

questions.question: In May 2025, which organization released the Global Report on Food Crises, highlighting rising hunger due to conflict and climate extremes?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Global Network Against Food Crises**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Global Network Against Food Crises** is an international alliance founded in 2016 by the **European Union (EU), Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO), and World Food Programme (WFP).**
 
• It aims to tackle food crises through coordinated humanitarian and development action, addressing the root causes of hunger and promoting food security worldwide.
 
• The **Global Report on Food Crises** is its flagship annual publication, which provides critical insights into the state of global food insecurity and its drivers, such as **conflict, climate extremes, and economic shocks.**
 
• The report for **May 2025** highlights a significant rise in hunger globally, attributing the alarming trend primarily to factors like **armed conflicts** and worsening **climate-related disasters.**
 
• The organization collaborates with multiple stakeholders, including governments, international agencies, and NGOs, to implement solutions and strategies that address both immediate needs and long-term stability.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO):**

 
 
• The **FAO** is a specialized agency of the United Nations that leads international efforts to defeat hunger.
 
• Established in **1945**, it focuses on improving agricultural productivity, ensuring food security, and promoting sustainable development in rural areas.
 
• Its work includes conducting research, publishing reports, and providing policy recommendations to governments and stakeholders.
 
 
 
• **World Bank:**
 
 
• The **World Bank** is an international financial institution established in **1944** to provide loans and grants to countries for development projects.
 
• Although it addresses poverty and economic development, its focus is broader than food crises, encompassing areas like education, infrastructure, and healthcare.
 
• It contributes to food security indirectly by funding projects aimed at agricultural innovation and rural development.
 
 
 
• **UN Environment Programme (UNEP):**
 
 
• The **UNEP** was founded in **1972** and focuses on the global environment, addressing issues such as climate change, biodiversity loss, and pollution.
 
• While it does not directly produce food-related reports, it highlights the environmental factors that impact agriculture and food security.
 
• UNEP emphasizes climate mitigation and adaptation to ensure sustainable ecosystems for food production.
 
 
 
• **Global Network Against Food Crises:**
 
 
• The network operates as a collaborative platform, bringing together humanitarian and development agencies to address food crises.
 
• It emphasizes data-driven decision-making, publishing the **Global Report on Food Crises** annually to guide policy interventions.
 
• Through partnerships, the network aims to reduce the number of people experiencing acute food insecurity and prevent future crises.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Drivers of Food Crises:**

 
 
• **Conflict:** Armed conflicts disrupt agricultural production, trade, and livelihoods, leading to food shortages and inflation.
 
• **Climate Extremes:** Events like droughts, floods, and hurricanes severely impact food production and availability.
 
• **Economic Shocks:** Inflation, unemployment, and reduced income levels exacerbate food insecurity, particularly in vulnerable populations.
 
 
 
• **Global Hunger Statistics:**
 
 
• As of **2025**, over **250 million people** globally are experiencing acute food insecurity due to the mentioned drivers.
 
• The regions most affected include **Sub-Saharan Africa, South Asia, and parts of the Middle East.**
 
• Women and children are disproportionately impacted, with long-term effects on health and development.
 
 
 
• **Collaborative Efforts:**
 
 
• Organizations like **FAO, WFP, and UNEP** work together to provide short-term relief and promote sustainable solutions.
 
• Innovative approaches include climate-resilient agriculture, disaster risk reduction, and improved food distribution systems.

questions.question: The Constitution (Scheduled Tribes) Order (Third Amendment) Bill, 2022, seeks to amend the Constitution (Scheduled Tribes) Order, 1950, with respect to its application to _____________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Himachal Pradesh**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The Constitution (Scheduled Tribes) Order (Third Amendment) Bill, 2022, seeks to amend the Constitution (Scheduled Tribes) Order, 1950, specifically for **Himachal Pradesh**.
 
• This amendment aims to include new communities under the category of **Scheduled Tribes** in Himachal Pradesh.
 
• The Constitution (Scheduled Tribes) Order, 1950, originally identified communities that qualify as Scheduled Tribes in different states and union territories of India.
 
• The inclusion or exclusion of communities under Scheduled Tribes is critical for ensuring access to **reserved benefits** such as educational quotas, job opportunities, and welfare schemes.
 
• The amendment reflects the government’s attempt to address the socio-economic and cultural needs of tribal communities in Himachal Pradesh by legally recognizing them.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Scheduled Tribes in India:**

 
 
• Scheduled Tribes are officially designated groups of people in India recognized as socially and economically disadvantaged.
 
• They are listed under Article 342 of the Indian Constitution, which gives the President the authority to specify Scheduled Tribes in consultation with the Governor of a state.
 
• India is home to over **705 Scheduled Tribes**, as per the 2011 Census.
 
• Benefits provided to Scheduled Tribes include reservation in education, employment, and legislative bodies, as well as specific welfare schemes.
 
 
 
• **Himachal Pradesh and Tribal Communities:**
 
 
• Himachal Pradesh is known for its diverse tribal population, including groups such as **Gaddis, Kinnauras, Gujjars, Pangwal, and Lahaulas**.
 
• Tribal communities in Himachal Pradesh primarily reside in remote areas, including **Lahaul-Spiti, Kinnaur, and Pangi**.
 
• These communities depend on agriculture, animal husbandry, and handicrafts for their livelihood.
 
• Efforts to include new communities aim to address the socio-economic challenges faced by these groups.
 
 
 
• **Constitutional Provisions for Scheduled Tribes:**
 
 
• Article 342 allows the President to declare tribes or tribal communities as Scheduled Tribes.
 
• Article 15 and Article 16 provide **reservation in education and employment** for Scheduled Tribes.
 
• Article 330 and Article 332 ensure **representation in the Lok Sabha and State Assemblies**.
 
• Article 46 directs the State to promote the educational and economic interests of Scheduled Tribes.
 
 
 
• **Amendment Process for Scheduled Tribes List:**
 
 
• The inclusion or exclusion of communities in the Scheduled Tribes list requires legislative approval through a constitutional amendment.
 
• The process involves consultation with the concerned state government and validation by the Parliament.
 
• Such amendments are critical for ensuring that identified tribes benefit from government schemes and legal protections.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Historical Context:**

 
 
• The Constitution (Scheduled Tribes) Order, 1950, was enacted to identify tribal communities across India.
 
• Several amendments have been introduced over the years to update the list of Scheduled Tribes based on evolving socio-political and cultural needs.
 
• These changes reflect the Indian government’s commitment to recognizing and addressing the challenges faced by indigenous communities.
 
 
 
• **Tribal Welfare Programs:**
 
 
• Programs such as the **Vanbandhu Kalyan Yojana** and Tribal Sub-Plan aim to improve the living standards of tribal communities.
 
• Special focus is given to education, healthcare, and employment under these schemes.
 
• Institutions like the **National Commission for Scheduled Tribes (NCST)** oversee the implementation of these welfare initiatives.

questions.question: The September 2025 guidelines on Anganwadi–School co-location emphasise which key component of child development?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Early Childhood Care and Education**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Early Childhood Care and Education (ECCE)** focuses on the holistic development of children during their formative years (0-6 years), including cognitive, emotional, social, and physical aspects.
 
• The **September 2025 guidelines on Anganwadi–School co-location** aim to integrate Anganwadi centers with schools to ensure a seamless transition and continuity in education for children.
 
• By co-locating Anganwadi centers and schools, the guidelines emphasize creating a strong foundation for **school readiness**, ensuring children are adequately prepared for formal schooling.
 
• The guidelines also focus on enhancing access to **quality early childhood education** for marginalized communities, addressing disparities in educational opportunities.
 
• This initiative aligns with the **National Education Policy (NEP) 2020**, which highlights ECCE as a critical factor in achieving universal foundational literacy and numeracy.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Importance of Early Childhood Care and Education (ECCE):**

 
 
• ECCE lays the foundation for lifelong learning, fostering **critical thinking**, creativity, and socio-emotional skills.
 
• Research highlights that the brain develops most rapidly during the first six years of life, making these years crucial for **cognitive and emotional growth**.
 
• Quality ECCE programs have been shown to improve **academic performance** and reduce dropout rates in later years.
 
• ECCE also plays a role in breaking the cycle of **poverty**, providing equitable opportunities to children from economically disadvantaged backgrounds.
 
 
 
• **Anganwadi Centers:**
 
 
• Established under the **Integrated Child Development Services (ICDS) scheme**, Anganwadi centers provide a range of services, including health, nutrition, and education, for children up to 6 years old.
 
• These centers focus on improving maternal and child health, ensuring adequate nutrition, and preparing children for school.
 
• There are approximately **1.37 million Anganwadi centers** across India as of 2023.
 
 
 
• **National Education Policy (NEP) 2020:**
 
 
• The NEP 2020 emphasizes universal access to ECCE by 2030 through the establishment of Anganwadi centers and pre-primary schools.
 
• It recommends the integration of **play-based and activity-based learning** approaches to enhance foundational literacy and numeracy.
 
• The policy also highlights teacher training and capacity building to improve the quality of ECCE programs.
 
 
 
• **Additional Government Initiatives for ECCE:**
 
 
• **Poshan Abhiyaan:** Focuses on improving nutritional outcomes for children, pregnant women, and lactating mothers.
 
• **Samagra Shiksha Abhiyan:** Supports school readiness and ECCE through infrastructure development and capacity building.
 
• **Saksham Anganwadi Scheme:** Aims to upgrade Anganwadi centers into modern resource hubs for ECCE and maternal health services.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Role of Teachers and Caregivers:**

 
 
• Teachers and Anganwadi workers are trained to deliver **age-appropriate educational content** and foster a nurturing environment.
 
• Continuous professional development programs ensure the adoption of **best practices** in ECCE.
 
 
 
• **Global Perspective on ECCE:**
 
 
• Countries like Finland and Sweden have successfully implemented robust ECCE systems, emphasizing play-based learning and holistic development.
 
• UNICEF advocates for universal access to ECCE as a strategy to achieve **Sustainable Development Goal 4** (Quality Education).
 
 
 
• **Challenges in ECCE Implementation:**
 
 
• Lack of infrastructure and resources in remote areas limits access to quality ECCE programs.
 
• Ensuring equitable access for marginalized communities remains a key challenge.

questions.question: As per the survey conducted by the Yale Program on Climate Change Communication and CVoter from 5 December 2024 to 18 February 2025, what percentage of Indians reported experiencing severe heatwaves in the past 12 months?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**0.71**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The survey was conducted by the **Yale Program on Climate Change Communication** in collaboration with **CVoter** between **5 December 2024** and **18 February 2025**.
 
• According to the survey, **71%** of Indians reported experiencing **severe heatwaves** in the past 12 months.
 
• The survey aimed to assess the **public perception** and **personal experiences** related to climate change and extreme weather conditions in India.
 
• The findings highlight the increasing **frequency and severity of heatwaves** in India, which is a direct impact of global climate change.
 
• This data emphasizes the urgent need for **climate adaptation and mitigation strategies** to address these extreme weather events.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Heatwaves:**

 
 
• A **heatwave** is a period of excessively hot weather, often accompanied by high humidity, which poses serious risks to health and the environment.
 
• In India, heatwaves are defined as a situation when the **maximum temperature** exceeds **40°C** in plains, **37°C** in coastal areas, and **30°C** in hilly regions.
 
• The frequency and intensity of heatwaves have increased in recent years due to **global warming** and **urban heat island effects**.
 
 
 
• **Impact of Heatwaves:**
 
 
• Heatwaves can lead to **heat-related illnesses** such as heatstroke, dehydration, and cardiovascular stress.
 
• They have significant impacts on **agriculture**, leading to **crop failure** and increased water demand.
 
• Prolonged heatwaves also strain **energy systems** due to higher demand for cooling and affect **livelihoods**, especially for outdoor workers.
 
 
 
• **India's Vulnerability:**
 
 
• India's geographical location and **tropical climate** make it highly susceptible to extreme weather events, including heatwaves.
 
• States like **Rajasthan**, **Uttar Pradesh**, **Maharashtra**, and **Telangana** frequently experience severe heat conditions.
 
• Urban areas, due to **concrete structures** and lack of vegetation, are more prone to higher temperatures.
 
 
 
• **Mitigation Measures:**
 
 
• The Indian government has implemented a **Heat Action Plan (HAP)** in several states to reduce the impact of heatwaves.
 
• Awareness campaigns, setting up **cooling centers**, and ensuring **adequate water supply** are part of HAP initiatives.
 
• Plantation drives, improving green cover, and using reflective building materials are long-term strategies to mitigate urban heat island effects.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Survey Methodology:** The survey conducted by Yale and CVoter utilized **random sampling techniques** to gather data from a representative sample of the Indian population.
 
• **Climate Awareness:** The survey also aimed to assess public awareness about **climate policies** and their support for measures like renewable energy adoption and carbon reduction initiatives.
 
• **Global Context:** Heatwaves are not unique to India; they are a global phenomenon, with regions like **Europe, Australia, and North America** also experiencing record-breaking temperatures in recent years.
 
• **Policy Implications:** The data from such surveys are crucial for informing **climate policies** and planning **disaster-resilient infrastructure**.

• **Policy Initiative:** The initiative is part of the **BioE3 Biotechnology policy**, which emphasizes leveraging biotechnology for advancements in space exploration, health sciences, and sustainability.
 
• **Collaborations:** The project aligns with global partnerships and cooperation in space research, contributing to India's efforts in enhancing its technological capabilities in space and biotechnology.

• Supports initiatives aimed at addressing **global challenges**, such as sustainable development and space exploration.
 
 
 
• **International Space Station (ISS):**
 
 
• The ISS is a collaborative space station involving **NASA**, **Roscosmos**, **ESA**, **JAXA**, and **CSA**.
 
• It serves as a hub for conducting **scientific research** in microgravity environments, including biological, physical, and astronomical studies.

• Studying biological adaptability in space is crucial for understanding the effects of **microgravity**, **radiation**, and **isolation** on human health.

• Biotechnology plays a vital role in addressing challenges related to **health**, **sustainability**, and **adaptability** during space missions.
 
• Experiments aboard the ISS help develop solutions for **space food production**, **regenerative medicine**, and **human survival** in extreme environments.
 
 
 
• **Global Impact:**
 
 
• India's involvement in ISS experiments underscores its commitment to contributing to **international scientific collaboration**.
 
• Findings from these studies have implications not only for space exploration but also for **earth-based applications** in biotechnology and medicine.

questions.question: What was the purpose of Operation Brahma launched by India in March 2025?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Earthquake relief**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Operation Brahma** was launched by **India in March 2025** as a dedicated mission aimed at providing **earthquake relief** in regions that were severely affected by a devastating earthquake.
 
• The operation was initiated in response to a **high-magnitude earthquake** that caused widespread destruction, including loss of life, damage to infrastructure, and displacement of populations.
 
• The primary objective of the operation was to provide **immediate humanitarian aid**, including rescue operations, medical assistance, and the distribution of food and essential supplies.
 
• The operation involved the collaboration of multiple agencies, including the **National Disaster Response Force (NDRF)**, **Indian Armed Forces**, and various non-governmental organizations (NGOs).
 
• Specialized teams were deployed to conduct **search-and-rescue missions** using advanced equipment and trained personnel to locate and save individuals trapped under rubble.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Earthquakes in India:**

 
 
• India is highly vulnerable to earthquakes, with over **59% of its landmass** prone to seismic activity. The regions are classified into **four seismic zones (Zone II, III, IV, and V)**.
 
• Zone V is the most seismically active region, covering areas like **Northeast India, parts of Jammu and Kashmir, Himachal Pradesh, Uttarakhand, and the Rann of Kutch in Gujarat.**
 
• Major earthquakes in Indian history include the **Bihar-Nepal earthquake (1934)**, **Latur earthquake (1993)**, **Bhuj earthquake (2001)**, and the **Kashmir earthquake (2005).**
 
 
 
• **National Disaster Response Force (NDRF):**
 
 
• The **NDRF** is a specialized force established under the **Disaster Management Act, 2005**, for disaster response and management in India.
 
• It operates under the Ministry of Home Affairs and is trained for **rescue, relief, and rehabilitation operations** during natural and man-made disasters.
 
• The force is equipped with state-of-the-art rescue equipment, including seismic sensors, life detectors, and cutting tools.
 
 
 
• **Indian Armed Forces in Disaster Relief:**
 
 
• The **Indian Armed Forces** play a critical role in disaster management, especially in large-scale emergencies like earthquakes, floods, and cyclones.
 
• They provide logistics, transportation, and **airlift operations** to deliver aid to inaccessible areas.
 
• For example, during the **Bhuj earthquake (2001)**, the Indian Army and Air Force led massive relief and rescue operations in Gujarat.
 
 
 
• **Disaster Preparedness in India:**
 
 
• The **National Disaster Management Authority (NDMA)** is the apex body responsible for formulating policies and guidelines for disaster management in India.
 
• India has also implemented early warning systems and conducts regular mock drills to enhance disaster preparedness.
 
• Community-based disaster risk reduction programs aim to educate and empower local populations to respond effectively during emergencies.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Earthquake Magnitude:** The magnitude of an earthquake is measured on the **Richter scale**, which quantifies the energy released by the seismic event.
 
• **Seismic Building Codes:** India has introduced **seismic-resistant building codes** to ensure that infrastructure is designed to withstand earthquakes, especially in high-risk areas.
 
• **International Cooperation:** India collaborates with global organizations like the **United Nations Office for Disaster Risk Reduction (UNDRR)** to enhance disaster resilience.
 
• **Key Initiatives:** Programs like the **Sendai Framework for Disaster Risk Reduction (2015-2030)** guide India’s strategies for reducing disaster risks and enhancing preparedness.
